items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: There’s a great record of Peggy Lee singing Cy Coleman’s “I’ve Got Your Number.”

ctx.x: Well I don’t know that I agree with that statement. I think that there is a way where music leans forward and leans backward. And we’re not machines. And even with a click track you can lean forward and it can be okay. And I always felt like there was some classic rhythm sections where the bass player might be a little ahead of the drummer, if you really put it up on a screen and analyzed it. And it feels unbelievable. And for whatever reason. I mean Ray Brown used to really drive hard with Oscar [Peterson] —…

you listen to Basie’s band, you know certain figures, they sit back. There’s a great record of Peggy Lee singing Cy Coleman’s “I’ve Got Your Number.” And there are a couple of horn figures where you can just hear — the lead trumpet player must have said, “we’re playing it like this.” And they just play the figure just a little more relaxed than the rest of the band is. And it’s great. I mean to me that’s the music.
Do you have any memories, when you were a kid, that you can think about now that you realized you had a sense of time and that you could feel grooves and feel the beat?
